recipes.name: Chicken Fiesta Salad
ingredients_raw: 1 (1.27 ounce) packet dry fajita seasoning, divided
1 (15 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Rub chicken evenly with 1/2 the fajita seasoning. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat, and cook the chicken 8 minutes on each side, or until juices run clear; set aside.
In a large saucepan, mix beans, corn, salsa and other 1/2 of fajita seasoning. Heat over medium heat until warm.
Prepare the salad by tossing the greens, onion and tomato. Top salad with chicken and dress with the bean and corn mixture.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Fiesta Salad
raw_recipe.description: Salad greens, onions and tomatoes are topped with Mexican flavored black beans, corn, and grilled chicken breasts. This is an attractive and zesty all in one dish.

video.description: Serve this up for a light dinner when you’re craving something a little spicy but not heavy! This chicken fiesta salad is the perfect combination!

review.reviewBody: This is one of our favorite summer meals. I use my own fajita seasoning, organic black beans and my own homemade salsa. This is also good with avocado. I like to mix the salsa with a tablespoon of sour cream with the salsa to make it stretch a little more and to make it creamy. This is a great way to stretch the little meat you do have on skinny week's before payday. To make it a little more filling, you can also add in cooked mexican rice. This makes a great filling for wraps, too.

Great for a quick and easy meal! I grilled my chicken vs. pan frying and used a homemade fajita seasoning. I used regular corn and left it cold as well as the beans. I also didn't bother adding any additional fajita seasoning. I added some Mexican blend cheese and some thin sliced avocado. I topped it off with a dollup of sour cream and some thin sliced green onion. This was great served with Ranch dressing and tortilla wedges on the side.

I made this recipe for the first time, and it's so healthy and delicious! Because I like to make things easier and faster, I cubed the chicken breasts, added 3 tsps of *homemade fajita seasoning* on here (minus the sodium) sautéed that til it was cooked most of the way. Then, in the same medium size sauce pan, I added the low sodium black beans, 12 oz thawed frozen corn, a can of no salt added Rotel, and three tsps more of the homemade fajita sauce. I simmered on low with lid on for an additional 15 mins, then served it warm over fresh greens. Delicious and so healthy! I always use low or no sodium for heart health, it doesn't need it at all, so flavorful! Also highly recommend making your own fajita seasoning and I quadrupled the recipe to have it on hand.

I chopped a bell pepper and added it to the corn bean salsa mix. Then served the salad with avocado and tortilla strips, sour cream optional. Also fried my spanish rice in the fajita seasoned oil left after cooking the chicken. My husband asked me to keep this recipe!

Yummo!!!! I took one persons idea, cutting the chicken breast into strips and marinated it in 1/2 the fajita seasoning and about 1 tablespoon olive oil. As the chicken cooked, I doused it with a little lime juice. To the salad, I added cilantro and chopped green bell pepper. I used thinly sliced purple onion. Everything else stayed the same. I served it with cheese quesadillas. To make these, I spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on one side of a tortilla put the tortilla in a non-stick frying pan - mayo side down, spread tortilla with shredded cheese, and cover with another tortilla with mayo spread on the outside. I toasted on both sides and cut into slices.

Awesome, and as others have indicated, a great salad to jump off on to create your own blend! I stirred the beans, corn and salsa right into the skillet with the chicken, and threw the onions into that mixture too. Added some grated marble cheese to the skillet as well which made the mixture all gooey and yummy! Grabbed some tortilla chips I had, crumbled them on top of the greens & tomatoes before layering on the chicken mixture. Added ranch dressing like others. Deeeeelishhhh!

I sauteed orange and yellow bell pepper with the onion, then added the corn, beans, salsa and seasoning. I even used chicken breasts that were already cooked. Just sliced them thin and warmed in a pan with fajita season and olive oil. I served this dish with sour cream.

This was tasty, and easy to make. A nice variation on salad, for those summer days. I diced the chicken in fajita seasoning and fresh garlic, and sprinkled onion powder & a little salt & pepper. I put this in one bowl. I put the bean & corn & salsa mix in a separate bowl. And the salad went in its own bowl. This way, people could make their own salad the way they wanted. For the salad--- I added cilantro, a small avocado, used a small red onion (not white onion), and added diced green bell pepper... they were all welcome flavors to the salad. I also had plain lowfat yogurt and shredded sharp cheddar cheese available, to "top" the salad with. I feel the yogurt & cheese also added good flavor to the salad. I think next time, I may use a little less onion, and just use some frozen corn (I didn't think it needed a full can of corn). Overall, a very nice dish and I'm sure I'll make it again!

This was pretty delicious. I went by the recipe and it made a nice lunch. I did mix up a combo of ranch mix, sour cream, and fresh cilantro to top it with. I also used green onions. I think this would be great in a tortilla bowl. Next time I won't heat up the salsa, bean, and corn mixture, and will omit the extra fajita seasoning. I think the salsa mixture would taste better left cold/room temp, when topping over the salad greens. Thanks for the recipe!

Chicken Fiesta Salad Haiku: "Colorful salad! Had to change just a few things. Tasty meal, ole!" I cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and marinated in the fajita seasoning mixed w/ a little EVOO and lime juice. After cooking the chicken, I didn't see the need to set it aside, so I simply tossed it w/ the beans, corn, salsa and additional seasoning so it was easier to serve. Doing so gave the chicken a bit more flavor, as it had a chance to simmer w/ the salsa/beans. Scooping the fiesta feast over baby spinach w/ red onion, tomatoes, grated cheddar and a handful of finely-chopped cilantro resulted in a vibrant, healthy, filling meal.
My kids LOVED this, can't wait to gave it again. I added capsicum to the salsa, cucumber to the salad and avocado on top. Chicken was so tender. So easy to throw together for a busy mid-week dinner.
This was great & super easy to make! Fun way to get a lot of leafy greens in for the day!

I loved this recipe. I made my own taco seasoning and used the taco seasoning recipe given . It is a much more wholesome seasoning than the store bought. The first night when serving the topping warm on top of the salad, it was more flavorful. The second night as leftovers, I needed to add salsa on top as it seemed dry the second night. Also, I added a dollop of sour cream and cubed an avocado to add a final touch of flavor (also looks pretty).
Omg, so good!! I followed the recipe to a T, added sliced avacado and a little ranch dressing to top. My family loved this, me, too! Healthy and hearty enough to stick to your ribs. This is a keeper!
My kids are picky eaters and they not only ate the chicken but also the salsa topping as well. Very good recipe
The recipe sounded good, but it turned out dry. It seemed like it was missing something.
This is a fantastic salad exactly as is!
Easy. Yummy. Dinner salad. I sautéed a little red pepper with the corn and beans. And used a packet of fajita seasoning and wished I used a jarred version instead.

Made it as the recipe stated and it was delicious and super easy/quick to make for a weekday dinner. I did not add cheese or tortilla chips and suggested in the description but next time I will try it.
